html:
Focus molecule
Which element sits at the vertex? Oxygen in Cl2O, chlorine in ClO2 — both are bent.
Bonding highlight
Click the low, forward vertex atom of a model (or any atom) to light up the two atoms bonded to it.
Guided demo
Radii used (van der Waals): Cl 175 pm (green) · O 152 pm (red) — identical in both panels, so the two models are directly comparable.
Drag to orbit (tilt limited ±40°), scroll to zoom — the vertex atom really does sit forward of the two outer atoms.

plan.chapterName: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, chapter 18: Representative Metals, Metalloids, and Nonmetals
plan.contextChunk: This figure places two space-filling molecular models side by side on a white ground, labeled "(a)" and "(b)" in small type beneath them. In model (a), two large green spheres each labeled "Cl" sit at the upper left and upper right, and a single red sphere labeled "O" is wedged between them and forward, sitting lower, so the three atoms describe a shallow V with the oxygen at the vertex. The spheres carry soft highlights and interpenetrate where the atoms are bonded, giving the fused outline of a space-filling representation rather than balls joined by sticks. Model (b) reverses the pattern: one large green sphere labeled "Cl" occupies the lower center and two red spheres labeled "O" rise from it at the upper left and upper right, again bent, this time with chlorine at the vertex. The red oxygens are noticeably smaller than the green chlorines, reflecting relative atomic size. Drawing both at one scale in one style asks the reader to compare which atom sits at the center and how many of each kind surround it. The pair are dichlorine monoxide and chlorine dioxide, the chlorine oxides used commercially for bleaching pulp and flour and for treating water.

elements: Panel (a) dichlorine monoxide Cl2O space-filling model
Two large green Cl spheres in panel (a), upper-left and upper-right, interpenetrating the central oxygen
One smaller red O sphere in panel (a) at the lower vertex, pushed forward toward the viewer
Black 'Cl' label on each green sphere in panel (a)
White 'O' label on the red sphere in panel (a)
Panel (b) chlorine dioxide ClO2 space-filling model
One large green Cl sphere in panel (b) at the lower-center vertex, pushed forward toward the viewer
Two smaller red O spheres in panel (b), upper-left and upper-right, set slightly back
White 'O' label on each red sphere in panel (b)
Black 'Cl' label on the green sphere in panel (b)
Soft specular highlight on the upper-left of every sphere
Caption '(a)' centered beneath the left model
Caption '(b)' centered beneath the right model
White background / no ground plane or shadow

interactions.label: Focus molecule
interactions.teaches: Swapping the formula swaps which element occupies the vertex: oxygen is central in Cl2O, chlorine is central in ClO2, while both stay bent.

Clicking the vertex atom lights up the two atoms bonded to it, showing that each molecule is one central atom with two identical outer atoms in a V arrangement, and that the green Cl sphere is always larger than the red O sphere.
Rotating reveals that the fused spheres are genuinely three-dimensional and bent, not a flat overlapping drawing — the vertex atom sits forward of the two outer atoms.

demo_steps.title: Both chlorine oxides
demo_steps.narration: Two space-filling models drawn at the same scale: the left is dichlorine monoxide, the right is chlorine dioxide. Green spheres are chlorine, red are oxygen, and the red spheres are visibly smaller.

demo_steps.title: (a) Cl2O — oxygen at the vertex
demo_steps.narration: In dichlorine monoxide the small red oxygen sits at the forward vertex with two large green chlorines above it, giving a shallow bent shape.

demo_steps.title: (b) ClO2 — chlorine at the vertex
demo_steps.narration: In chlorine dioxide the roles reverse: one large green chlorine occupies the vertex and two smaller red oxygens rise from it, again bent.

demo_steps.title: Compare the centers
demo_steps.narration: Returning to the pair, the only structural difference is which element sits at the center and which two flank it — both molecules are V-shaped triatomics.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Scale: 1 world unit = 100 pm. Sphere radii use van der Waals values — Cl radius 1.75, O radius 1.52 (O spheres clearly smaller than Cl). Panel (a) centered at x = -3.2, panel (b) at x = +3.2; both models roughly 5 units wide, whole scene spans about x ∈ [-6.5, 6.5], y ∈ [-3, 3]. Model (a) Cl2O: bond length Cl–O = 1.70, bond angle Cl–O–Cl = 110.9°. Place the red O at the vertex low and forward — local coords O = (0, -0.9, +0.7); the two green Cl at (-1.35, +0.45, -0.15) and (+1.35, +0.45, -0.15). Spheres interpenetrate strongly (center distance 1.70 < sum of radii 3.27) so the outline reads as a fused blob, with the forward red sphere overlapping in front of the green ones along their lower inner edges, exactly as in the source. Model (b) ClO2: bond length Cl–O = 1.47, bond angle O–Cl–O = 117.4°. Green Cl at the vertex low and forward — local coords Cl = (0, -0.75, +0.6); red O spheres at (-1.25, +0.45, -0.1) and (+1.25, +0.45, -0.1), set slightly back so the green sphere's rounded top pushes forward between them. Both models bend upward (vertex atom lowest, outer atoms raised). Colors: chlorine green with a light-to-mid gradient, base #3CA83C with highlight toward #8DD35F; oxygen red base #D91F1F with highlight toward #F26B6B. Labels: 'Cl' in black bold sans on green spheres, 'O' in white bold sans on red spheres, always drawn facing the camera and centered on the visible face of each sphere. Captions '(a)' and '(b)' in small dark gray text at y = -3.0 beneath each model. Background pure white, no shadow or ground plane.
interactionPlan.notes: Use THREE.SphereGeometry (32+ segments) with MeshPhongMaterial or MeshStandardMaterial (low roughness, modest specular) to reproduce the airbrushed space-filling highlight; one key directional light from the upper-left plus soft ambient/hemisphere fill so each sphere shows a single bright spot at its upper-left, matching the source. No outlines, no bond cylinders — overlap of opaque spheres does the work. Render atom labels as CSS2DObject/sprite text anchored to each sphere center and offset toward the camera so they never get z-buried by the sphere surface; keep label size constant in screen space. Panel captions as fixed 2D HTML overlays under each model. For 'focus' toggle, animate the unfocused molecule's material opacity down to ~0.18 (transparent, depthWrite false) and slightly scale/center the focused one; camera dollies from the wide two-panel framing to the single molecule. Click highlighting: raycast against sphere meshes, and on hitting the vertex atom apply an emissive tint plus a thin outward-scaled backface shell to the two bonded spheres. Orbit should be limited in elevation (±40°) so the figure keeps its recognizable front-on reading.

authoredContext:
As a class, the oxides are extremely reactive and unstable, and their chemistry has little practical importance. Dichlorine oxide, formally called dichlorine monoxide, and chlorine dioxide, both shown in the figure, are the only commercially important compounds. They are important as bleaching agents (for use with pulp and flour) and for water treatment.

This image shows the structures of the (a) Cl2O and (b) ClO2 molecules.

Two space filling models are shown and labeled, “a,” and “b.” Model a shows a red atom labeled, “O,” bonded to two green atoms labeled, “C l,” in a v-shape. Model b shows a green atom labeled, “C l,” bonded to two red atoms labeled, “O,” in a v-shape.

discrepancies: Sphere colors are noticeably darker/duller than the source's bright kelly green and vivid red, giving the models a muddier look.
A secondary grey/white specular blob from the fill light appears on the lower-right of each sphere, an artifact not present in the source's single airbrushed highlight.
Atom labels ('Cl', 'O') are considerably smaller relative to the spheres than the large bold typography in the source figure, weakening the label hierarchy.
In (b) the two red oxygens are rendered visibly smaller than in the source, where the outer O spheres read nearly as large as the central Cl.
evaluation.notes: Composition, bent geometry, vertex-atom placement and depth ordering closely match the source, with strong, pedagogically meaningful interactions (focus toggles, bonded-atom highlight, 4-step guided tour); main weaknesses are duller colors, a stray second specular highlight, and undersized atom labels.
action_items: Brighten the palette toward the source (e.g. green ~#4CBB3C/#5CC24E, red ~#E8241F) and increase ambient so the spheres read as saturated as the original.
Reduce or reposition the fill light so each sphere shows one airbrushed highlight in the upper-left, eliminating the grey lower-right blob.
Increase atom label font size (roughly 1.5×) and add a subtle text shadow so 'Cl' and 'O' dominate visually like the source's bold caps; keep '(a)'/'(b)' captions smaller.
Nudge the outer O radii in model (b) slightly larger (or the central Cl slightly smaller) so the size relationship matches the source's proportions while preserving the Cl>O ordering.

feedback.rationale: Concept, structure, and interactions are correct; remaining issues are implementation details (consistent per-element radii, brighter colors/highlights, geometry offset, larger captions) best fixed in rendering.

plan.contextChunk: This figure places two space-filling molecular models side by side on a white ground, labeled "(a)" and "(b)" in small type beneath them. In model (a), two large green spheres each labeled "Cl" sit at the upper left and upper right, and a single red sphere labeled "O" is wedged between them and forward, sitting lower, so the three atoms describe a shallow V with the oxygen at the vertex. The spheres carry soft highlights and interpenetrate where the atoms are bonded, giving the fused outline of a space-filling representation rather than balls joined by sticks. Model (b) reverses the pattern: one large green sphere labeled "Cl" occupies the lower center and two red spheres labeled "O" rise from it at the upper left and upper right, again bent, this time with chlorine at the vertex. The red oxygens are noticeably smaller than the green chlorines, reflecting relative atomic size. Drawing both at one scale in one style asks the reader to compare which atom sits at the center and how many of each kind surround it. The pair are dichlorine monoxide and chlorine dioxide, the chlorine oxides used commercially for bleaching pulp and flour and for treating water.

interactions.label: Focus molecule
interactions.teaches: Swapping the formula swaps which element occupies the vertex: oxygen is central in Cl2O, chlorine is central in ClO2, while both stay bent.

Clicking the vertex atom lights up the two atoms bonded to it, showing that each molecule is one central atom with two identical outer atoms in a V arrangement, and that the green Cl sphere is always larger than the red O sphere.
Rotating reveals that the fused spheres are genuinely three-dimensional and bent, not a flat overlapping drawing — the vertex atom sits forward of the two outer atoms.

demo_steps.title: Both chlorine oxides
demo_steps.narration: Two space-filling models drawn at the same scale: the left is dichlorine monoxide, the right is chlorine dioxide. Green spheres are chlorine, red are oxygen, and the red spheres are visibly smaller.

demo_steps.title: (a) Cl2O — oxygen at the vertex
demo_steps.narration: In dichlorine monoxide the small red oxygen sits at the forward vertex with two large green chlorines above it, giving a shallow bent shape.

demo_steps.title: (b) ClO2 — chlorine at the vertex
demo_steps.narration: In chlorine dioxide the roles reverse: one large green chlorine occupies the vertex and two smaller red oxygens rise from it, again bent.

demo_steps.title: Compare the centers
demo_steps.narration: Returning to the pair, the only structural difference is which element sits at the center and which two flank it — both molecules are V-shaped triatomics.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Scale: 1 world unit = 100 pm. Sphere radii use van der Waals values — Cl radius 1.75, O radius 1.52 (O spheres clearly smaller than Cl). Panel (a) centered at x = -3.2, panel (b) at x = +3.2; both models roughly 5 units wide, whole scene spans about x ∈ [-6.5, 6.5], y ∈ [-3, 3]. Model (a) Cl2O: bond length Cl–O = 1.70, bond angle Cl–O–Cl = 110.9°. Place the red O at the vertex low and forward — local coords O = (0, -0.9, +0.7); the two green Cl at (-1.35, +0.45, -0.15) and (+1.35, +0.45, -0.15). Spheres interpenetrate strongly (center distance 1.70 < sum of radii 3.27) so the outline reads as a fused blob, with the forward red sphere overlapping in front of the green ones along their lower inner edges, exactly as in the source. Model (b) ClO2: bond length Cl–O = 1.47, bond angle O–Cl–O = 117.4°. Green Cl at the vertex low and forward — local coords Cl = (0, -0.75, +0.6); red O spheres at (-1.25, +0.45, -0.1) and (+1.25, +0.45, -0.1), set slightly back so the green sphere's rounded top pushes forward between them. Both models bend upward (vertex atom lowest, outer atoms raised). Colors: chlorine green with a light-to-mid gradient, base #3CA83C with highlight toward #8DD35F; oxygen red base #D91F1F with highlight toward #F26B6B. Labels: 'Cl' in black bold sans on green spheres, 'O' in white bold sans on red spheres, always drawn facing the camera and centered on the visible face of each sphere. Captions '(a)' and '(b)' in small dark gray text at y = -3.0 beneath each model. Background pure white, no shadow or ground plane.
interactionPlan.notes: Use THREE.SphereGeometry (32+ segments) with MeshPhongMaterial or MeshStandardMaterial (low roughness, modest specular) to reproduce the airbrushed space-filling highlight; one key directional light from the upper-left plus soft ambient/hemisphere fill so each sphere shows a single bright spot at its upper-left, matching the source. No outlines, no bond cylinders — overlap of opaque spheres does the work. Render atom labels as CSS2DObject/sprite text anchored to each sphere center and offset toward the camera so they never get z-buried by the sphere surface; keep label size constant in screen space. Panel captions as fixed 2D HTML overlays under each model. For 'focus' toggle, animate the unfocused molecule's material opacity down to ~0.18 (transparent, depthWrite false) and slightly scale/center the focused one; camera dollies from the wide two-panel framing to the single molecule. Click highlighting: raycast against sphere meshes, and on hitting the vertex atom apply an emissive tint plus a thin outward-scaled backface shell to the two bonded spheres. Orbit should be limited in elevation (±40°) so the figure keeps its recognizable front-on reading.

discrepancies: Sphere colours are noticeably darker/duller than the source: the source uses a bright yellow-green (≈#5CBE28) and a vivid scarlet, while the render uses a deeper forest green (#3CA83C) and a darker brick red (#D91F1F).

Specular treatment differs: the source shows a broad soft gradient sheen on each sphere, whereas the render shows small hard white/pink hot-spots, which reads as shinier plastic than the matte airbrushed spheres of the original.

In the source panel (b) the two red oxygens are nearly the same apparent diameter as the central chlorine; the render enforces true vdW radii so the red spheres read distinctly smaller, a slight deviation from the source proportions (though chemically more correct).

The vertex atom in panel (a) of the source projects further downward/forward, giving the characteristic teardrop silhouette; the render's O sits slightly higher and is more fully occluded by the two Cl spheres.
